text.p: Bonds closed sharply higher, with the June futures expiring at a record, and some traders saw room for the cash spread with the 10-year Bund to narrow.
Traders noted that there was a huge gap between the September futures and the 10-year cash which needed to be closed one way or the other.

The motive for the market's surge was the accord reached by the European Union that appeared to have ended the argument between the new French government and Germany over how to proceed with monetary union.
"The 10-year cash consolidated at around 70 basis points to the Bund but it could test lower levels tomorrow," said one trader. director.
"The OTs (bonds) closed buyer and could gain up to five basis points on the Bund (10-years), keeping neutral against the (Spanish) Bonos," added another trader.
But the yield curve did not steepen because short-term money has still not fallen sufficiently.

However, if May inflation figures came in close to 1.5 percent year-on-year when they are announced on Tuesday, short rates will definitely ease as this will be taken as a signal that the Bank of Portugal can cut rates again, traders said.
Analysts have predicted a rate of between 1.4 and 1.8 percent.
Forward-rate agreements (FRA) fell between eight and 10 basis points, with September standing at 5.16/21 and December at 4.96/5.01 percent.
